The name La Rochelle means "the little rock". 
Rupella: First recorded in Latin in 961 AD as Rupella, a diminutive form of rupis (rock).
Rochelle: Evolved through Old French (rochelle) and Old Occitan (La Rochela), stemming from roche (rock), derived from Late Latin rocca, combined with the feminine diminutive suffix -elle (little).
La: The French definite article meaning "the". 
The name describes the city's original geography: a small, rocky natural elevation and fortified outcrop rising above the surrounding coastal marshes and Atlantic Ocean. 

Little Rock is the capital and most populous city of the U.S. state of Arkansas. The population was 202,591 at the 2020 census, while the Little Rock metropolitan area with an estimated 770,000 residents is the 81st-most populous metropolitan area in the United States.[4] The city lies on the south bank of the Arkansas River close to the state's geographic center in central Arkansas. It is the county seat of Pulaski County.

Little Rock was founded in 1821 as the capital of the Arkansas Territory. It is named for a rock formation along the Arkansas River named the "Little Rock" by the French explorer Jean-Baptiste Bénard de la Harpe in 1722. The city played a notable role in U.S. history during the 1957 desegregation of Little Rock Central High School, a key event in the Civil Rights movement. Little Rock is a cultural, economic, government, and transportation center within Arkansas and the American South.

Economically, Little Rock is supported by a mix of sectors including healthcare, banking, transportation, and retail. Companies such as Dillard's and Windstream Holdings are headquartered in the city, and the University of Arkansas for Medical Sciences contributes to its healthcare industry and academic research. Its cultural sites include the Arkansas Museum of Fine Arts, Clinton Presidential Center, and Quapaw Quarter. Outdoor spaces such as the Arkansas River Trail and Pinnacle Mountain State Park provide recreational opportunities within and near the city.

Friday the 13th 
"Friday-the-13th" has since entered the culture as a "bad omen" day. The Priory of Sion did not in ignorance choose Friday-the-13th for their attack upon the Templars. Well aware of the significance the Templars placed on the esoteric value of this number (its Order contained 13 degrees), the Priory must have realized the debilitating effect an attack on this day would have. King Philip, on the other hand, was probably less discerning. All he wanted was the Templars' immense wealth, which eluded him. It was never found, which is strange indeed, for in Paris was the Templars' central bank for all Europe. The preceptory there would have stored the largest cache of gold, second only to that which was allegedly hidden at Rennes-le-Chateau.

Another Double-Cross? 
Had the Priory of Sion double-crossed King Philip, too? Circumstantial evidence supports this conclusion. For instance, throughout the period of this intrigue, Guillaume Pidoye - one of the king's men and guardian and administrator of the Templar goods at the Paris preceptory after the arrest of the Templars - was also a colleague of Guillaume de Gisors, the Grand Master of Sion. If Pidoye was himself a Sionist, which seems to have been the case, he would certainly have been more loyal to his Grand Master than to the King.

The Holy Blood authors also suggest that Pidoye acted as a "double agent," warning the Templars of their impending arrest at the Paris preceptory. This would appear to have been an act of treason against both the king and Sion. According to legend, sometime before Fridaythe- 13th, the treasury in the preceptory, together with almost all its documents and records, was transported to the Templar naval base at LaRochelle, and loaded into eighteen galleys, which were never heard of again.

Why would Pidoye warn the Templars? It is unlikely he would warn the enemy of his Sionist Grand Master. He would more likely inform Guillaume de Gisors of the King's impending move against the Templars.

The authors of Holy Blood hint at another explanation when they suggest that the Grand Master of Sion "might have been partially responsible for.. .the unexplained disappearance of its treasure."

Alerting the Templars would then be part of an intricately woven plan. Pidoye may not have been a "double agent" as has been suggested, but a "triple agent." Pidoye knew Sion had no means of transporting Templar gold to the coast. Nor had they any ships. Only the Knights Templar had means of transport, with a fleet at La Rochelle. If tipped off in advance, the Knights could reach the port city in time. Pidoye, as representative of the king, would feign sympathy toward the Templars, warning them of impending danger, suggesting they transport their wealth out of the country before Friday-the-13th. As a triple agent, he would then inform the Grand Master of Sion of the gold transport. The Priory in turn would instruct its protector, the English navy, to intercept and scuttle the ships after confiscating the gold. The gold would then be taken to England.

What can change is your class position (your relation to property and labour) and your class standpoint (whose interests you organize your life around) but the test is not mere declaration. You have to make a genuine "break" with the class of your origin.

Intellectual break. Seeing that your own class’s interests rest on exploitation, and that your emancipation is tied to abolishing class society rather than climbing within it.

Material break. Conviction alone proves little. Amilcar Cabral called this “class suicide”: giving up privilege, property, security and career, and accepting the risks that the working class faces. Without it, the position remains bourgeois even when the language is revolutionary.

Organizational subordination. The most reliable test is whether the person accepts discipline and accountability to a working-class base and its organization, rather than leading as a benevolent patron. Gramsci’s idea of the “organic intellectual” fits here: someone who emerges from and is answerable to a class, rather than floating above it.

Immersion and re-education. Mao insisted that intellectuals had to learn from workers and peasants through shared work and life. Habits of speech, assumptions, ease with authority, and a sense of entitlement outlast ideological conversion, which is why Bourdieu’s point about habitus matters.

Time and proof. Credibility is earned through years of conduct, especially under pressure, not by declaration.

Those who defect from the bourgeoisie can slide into substitutionism, speaking for the working class instead of building its capacity to speak for itself, and into paternalism. Many socialist movements have also been damaged by leaders whose privilege reasserted itself once they held power. That’s why movements place so much weight on collective control and accountability instead of trusting personal virtue.

In India there is a further layer. Dr. Ambedkar’s critique of the Left was that upper-caste leaders could shed class privilege in theory while carrying caste privilege untouched, in networks, assumptions, and who gets heard and trusted. So the break has to be a caste break as well as a class break, and where it isn’t, the working-class base is correct to be suspicious. This is part of why the Bahujan tradition emphasizes leadership emerging from the oppressed themselves rather than being delivered from above.

The upshot is that origin is not destiny, but class change is a process of material sacrifice and accountable practice rather than a single act of conversion.

Prizor's success will depend on converting its manufacturing investments and distribution network into sustainable revenue and cash flow. The company needs to increase capacity utilisation, expand its dealer network and strengthen its presence in institutional markets. It should also focus on developing higher value products rather than competing only on price.Successful development of its indigenous semiconductor chip could strengthen its competitive position, but the company must first demonstrate that the technology is commercially viable. Most importantly, revenue growth should translate into higher profits and stronger operating cash flow.
A business that grows rapidly while continuously increasing debt may struggle to create long term shareholder value.

The commissioning of Prizor's additional manufacturing capacity in July 2026 marks an important transition from expansion plans to actual execution. The company has increased annual assembly capacity from 16 lakh units to 24 lakh units.
This is significant because Prizor has already demonstrated strong demand and revenue growth. The next stage is to convert its expanded manufacturing capacity into higher sales, profits and cash flow. The indigenous semiconductor chip could eventually become an even bigger technological turning point. However, the most important development to monitor today is whether Prizor can successfully utilise its expanded manufacturing capacity while maintaining margins and controlling working capital.

Prizor Viztech is therefore attempting to transform itself from an import driven surveillance brand into a more integrated Indian manufacturer. Its rapid revenue growth, expanding dealer network, healthy margins and manufacturing investments are encouraging. The biggest opportunities lie in increasing manufacturing utilisation, benefiting from domestic surveillance demand, expanding into higher value AI products and reducing dependence on imported components. However, the company is still much smaller than established competitors and faces meaningful working capital, debt and execution risks. The key question for investors is no longer whether Prizor can grow its revenue. It is whether the company can convert that growth into sustainable profits and strong cash generation.

Demanding Valuation:

At nearly 69 times earnings, the market is already pricing in substantial future growth.
Prizor's business prospects are encouraging, but the stock is no longer available at a modest valuation. The market is already assigning a premium to its growth potential. The key question is whether the company can grow its profits fast enough to justify this premium.
Strong execution could support the valuation, but any disappointment in revenue growth, margins or working capital could lead to a sharp correction.

From an Import Driven Brand to an Indian Surveillance Manufacturer

Business Model:

Prizor Viztech designs, manufactures and sells CCTV cameras, video recorders and other surveillance equipment under its own brand.

Its products reach customers through a network of more than 11,000 dealers across 21 to 22 states. These dealers supply local installers, shops and institutional customers.This distribution model allows Prizor to expand its reach without having to establish its own retail outlets across the country.

The company also sells televisions, monitors and touch panels but these are manufactured by third party partners. Surveillance products remain its main business.

The biggest change is that Prizor is gradually moving from importing components and assembling cameras towards manufacturing more of its products in India. Its Gandhinagar facility includes circuit board assembly, plastic housing moulding, camera manufacturing and laser branding. This allows the company to control more of the manufacturing process and potentially retain a larger share of the value created.

Prizor has grown rapidly over the last three years. Revenue increased from approximately ₹13.8 crore in FY23 to ₹147.94 crore in FY26. Net profit increased from just ₹30 lakh to ₹20.76 crore during the same period. Its dealer network has more than doubled in two years, increasing from approximately 5,200 dealers to over 11,000. CCTV camera sales grew 152% during FY26, reflecting the increasing contribution of its core business.

The company reported an EBITDA margin of 22.5% in FY26, while its H1 FY27 EBITDA margin improved to 23.6%. Its H1 FY27 revenue increased 153% to ₹106.5 crore, while net profit grew 159% to ₹15.3 crore.
The company has also commissioned an additional assembly line, increasing annual assembly capacity from 16 lakh units to 24 lakh units.

Prizor's biggest competitive advantage is the combination of its own manufacturing facility, expanding dealer network and certifications required for selling surveillance products in India.
The government has introduced stricter certification requirements for surveillance equipment. This creates an opportunity for domestic manufacturers that can meet the required standards.

Prizor has obtained BIS and STQC related certifications for multiple camera models.
However, certification alone does not guarantee market leadership. Larger competitors such as CP Plus and Hikvision India also have certified products.

Prizor is not a monopoly and is not the market leader. Its CCTV revenue of approximately ₹114 crore in FY26 represents only a small share of the Indian surveillance market.

Its reported margins suggest that it can earn reasonable profits, but this does not necessarily mean it has strong pricing power.

The surveillance industry remains competitive, and customers can choose from several brands.

Aditya Infotech, which owns the CP Plus brand, is also listed in India. Prizor is listed on the NSE SME platform and is much smaller than established competitors.
Its opportunity is to build a stronger position by offering reliable products, expanding distribution and increasing local manufacturing.

Profit growth is not yet translating into strong cash generation. Prizor reported FY26 net profit of ₹20.76 crore, but operating cash flow was only approximately ₹29 lakh.This suggests that a significant amount of money is getting tied up in inventory and customer receivables.
The company needs to demonstrate that its growth can generate cash, not just accounting profits.

Working capital requirements are increasing.Short term borrowings reportedly increased from ₹2.8 crore to ₹31.8 crore. This is important because rapid growth can become difficult to sustain if the company has to borrow heavily to finance inventory and dealer credit.

📢 A MESSAGE SPECIFICALLY FOR RETAIL INVESTORS!

Stop getting satisfied with 20%, 30%, 40% or even 50% returns. Start thinking BIG. I'm talking about identifying potential 5X–10X opportunities, especially 8X–10X multibaggers.

Why?

Because 30–40% of your investment bets may fail, some may deliver average returns, and a few exceptional winners can make a significant difference to your overall portfolio.

But understand this: 2–3 stocks delivering 8X–10X returns can make a huge difference in a 15-stock portfolio. The same may not be true for a portfolio of 40–50 stocks.

In fact, the chances of identifying and holding those exceptional winners may be lower in a 40–50 stock portfolio, particularly when the portfolio is built without deep research and conviction in each business.

You need to research deeply, identify a few exceptional opportunities and understand the businesses you own.

Now, understand the difference between PREEMPTORS and REACTORS.

Where preemptors start booking profits, reactors often start buying. When a stock becomes popular and everyone starts talking about it, I personally start becoming cautious.

Let's take the example of Prizor Viztech.

In my opinion, many investors started noticing the opportunity only when I had already begun booking profits gradually.

My approach is simple: when the broader market starts discovering and buying a stock, I may already be looking at partial profit booking. I understand the sector, I understand the business, and I try to anticipate rather than react.

And remember, exceptional returns don't come from reacting to premium news or quarterly results.

They come from identifying a good company in a promising sector, buying it at an attractive valuation with good management, or playing a genuine turnaround story.

These returns will not come from reacting to quarterly results. They come from understanding businesses and anticipating opportunities.

I hope you are learning the difference.

BE A PREEMPTOR, NOT A REACTOR.

There is no shortcut in the market. Understand the business. Understand the sector. Do your own research.

Nou, lieve Europese belastingbetalers, schuif die stoelen maar even aan, want de EU heeft weer eens een aflevering van Circus Zonder Toezicht geopend. 

Denemarken geeft Estland geld om munitie voor Oekraïne te kopen. Maar waar belandt die 71 miljoen Deense kroon, ongeveer 9,5 miljoen euro? Bij een Italiaans bedrijf genaamd Datasel. En wat levert dat bedrijf? Helemaal niks! Geen kogels, geen granaten, geen munitie, nog geen rotte patroonhuls!

En nu wordt het pas echt mahala babyy..

Dat Italiaanse bedrijf hield zich eerder bezig met softwareontwikkeling, zat op hetzelfde adres als een Audi dealer en had niet eens de vergunningen om wapens te produceren of te verkopen. De militaire catalogus? Afbeeldingen uit videogames en AI plaatjes! Haha.. 

Dus ergens in de EU heeft iemand gedacht.. kijk eens, wat een indrukwekkende wapenleverancier! Die man kan blijkbaar een tank verkopen die alleen in een computerspel bestaat, maar laten we hem alvast 9,5 miljoen euro overmaken!

Mijn hemel, wat een bestuurlijke acrobatiek. In ut kamp noemen we dat geen wapenhandel, maar een digitale goocheltruc met andermans portemonnee.

En het mooiste? Estland had eerder al te maken gehad met afgezegde leveringen door datzelfde bedrijf, maar stuurde toch opnieuw geld. Dat is geen aanbesteding meer, dat is een blind date met een pinautomaat!

Denemarken wil inmiddels het geld terug en er loopt een onderzoek. Kijk eens aan, ineens heeft de EU ontdekt dat geld ook terug kan moeten komen. Wat een revolutionaire uitvinding!

Maar wacht even… de EU staat ondertussen met opgeheven vingertje tegen de rest van de wereld te preken over transparantie, democratie, rechtsstaat en verantwoord bestuur. Ze willen overal toezicht houden, overal regels opleggen en overal de boekhouding controleren.

Alleen hun eigen geld verdwijnt blijkbaar in een Italiaanse spookwinkel waar de munitie uitsluitend op een computerscherm bestaat.

De Europese belastingbetaler betaalt dus voor kogels die nooit zijn geleverd, bij een bedrijf dat niet eens bevoegd was om ze te leveren. De enige die hier raak geschoten heeft, is degene die de factuur heeft verstuurd!

En dan vragen ze zich af waarom mensen het vertrouwen in Brussel verliezen.

Lieve schatten, als dit de Europese manier van oorlog voeren is, hebben ze straks geen vijand meer nodig. Ze schieten zichzelf financieel volledig aan flarden!

De EU.. miljarden voor wapens, miljoenen voor luchtkastelen en als eindresultaat.. een lege patroonhuls met een Audi logo erop.

67 IPOs. One request to SEBI on behalf of us all.

A humble request: Please repost this until it becomes a regulatory amendment.

Imagine being a 20–30-year-old direct equity investing enthusiast, building a portfolio with the ambition of creating generational wealth over the next few decades...

Between 2024 and October 2026, we identified 67 mainboard IPOs that were subscribed over 5× and, at some point since listing, traded at least 100% above their IPO issue price.

Yes some have corrected significantly since then.

That's not the point.

These 67 IPOs could have been opportunities for young investors like me to begin building long-term ownership in selective businesses.

But overwhelming subscription demand meant many of us couldn't secure allotments.

And after listing, valuations, limited monthly cash flows or other circumstances kept us from entering.

As long-term investors, we think in decades, not quarters.

We have anchor allocations for institutional investors, including mutual funds.

But there is no comparable dedicated allocation for individual investors willing to commit their capital for the long term.

Why can't a small portion of IPO shares be reserved for long-term retail investors who voluntarily commit to a defined lock-in period?

I request SEBI and the concerned regulators to consider such an amendment, with transparent eligibility and appropriate safeguards.

Help us build ownership, not just access to trading.

These 67 IPOs illustrate the opportunities that many young investors could have participated in.

Hmm… methinks you didn’t read the closing chapters of Harry Potter and Deathly Hallows very closely. Either that, or the depiction of these events in the film have caused you to forget how things happened in the book.

One of the biggest, most patently annoying changes made in the Deathly Hallows Part 2 film was the decision not to evacuate the students and, instead, have the battle unfold while Hogwarts is filled with hundreds of children aged 11–16. The presence of young kids would have made the battle patently impossible for the defenders to win, because they would have been forced to surrender: The youngsters would be, essentially, an unstable element that would have thrown any defensive plans into chaos when they inevitably panicked.

In the book, almost every student below the age of 17 was evacuated through the Room of Requirement, via the same secret passage to the Hog’s Head cellar that the trio used to get back into the school. I say almost every studentbecause Colin Creevey, the 11-year-old photographer from Chamber of Secrets, 16-years-old by then, managed to sneak away from the evacuation and participated in the battle. Sadly, he was killed in the fighting.

In the book, of the 17-year-old students, all from Slytherin, most from Ravenclaw, half from Hufflepuff and none from Gryffindor voluntarily evacuated with the underage students.

Thus, the defenders of Hogwarts, in the book, consisted of:

•a few dozen 7th Year students from Gryffindor, Hufflepuff and Ravenclaw
•several members of Dumbledore’s Army that had already graduated (who were summoned by Neville via their enchanted Protean coins)

•several older former students that the DA members notified (such as Gryffindor former team captains Oliver Wood and Angelina Johnson)

•the entire Order of the Phoenix (which was somewhat more sizable than the films portrayed, lots of small-name Order members never reached the screen)

•Neville Longbottom’s grandmother and Percy Weasley arrived via the Room of Requirement part way through the battle. Thanks Louis Juliot for pointing this out.

•and the school staff with the exception of the Carrows, who were bound and trussed inside the Ravenclaw Common Room

I should say that, by the same token, there weren’t nearlyas many Death Eaters assaulting the school as the film portrayed. The film showed hundreds of attacking Death Eaters, and nearly a thousand “Snatchers” attacking from the rear (excuse me a moment while I go and add that to Sean Thomas' answer to In the Harry Potter series, which director deviated the most from book to movie?). Seriously, there aren’t enough wizards and witches living in Britain for there to be that many Snatchers and Death Eaters.
I digress.

So, in the book and film, Harry went to the forest and sacrificed himself. Voldemort, believing Harry dead, took his “corpse” and his remaining Death Eaters and approached the front gates of the school. So far, the film and the book is the same (except that there was no bridge to the front gate in the book, the castle had a very large, sloped lawn).
Voldemort, backed by his Death Eaters, mocked the remaining defenders of Hogwarts and attempted to bully them into surrendering. Neville approached Voldemort.

Now the film and book diverge greatly.

The book version of the Battle of Hogwarts portrays a community-driven victory rooted in Harry's sacrifice, whereas the film alters the scale and strips away the story's core message. Unlike the film's inflated enemy numbers, the book features a smaller, realistic Death Eater force that is ultimately overwhelmed when Hogsmeade villagers, students' parents, and house-elves arrive to reinforce the castle. 

Furthermore, the book emphasizes that Harry’s sacrifice placed a protective shield over the defenders, rendering Voldemort’s spells useless, which allowed a fiery Neville to break free and decapitate Nagini, proving that Voldemort's army would have been utterly defeated even if Harry hadn't survived.

Dánská vláda zaplatila falešné firmě 71 milionů korun za granáty pro Ukrajinu

Místo toho, aby Dánsko posílalo na Ukrajinu dělostřelecké granáty, nakonec poslalo "velkou tašku s penězi" společnosti, která na svých webových stránkách používala obrázky z počítačových her a sdílela adresu s prodejcem Audi.

Základna Ramstein byla sídlem pracovní skupiny spojenců Ukrajiny, nejčastěji jednoduše nazývané „skupina Ramstein“.

A právě zde na schůzce požádal estonský ministr obrany Hanno Pevkur jednoho dne v březnu 2024 Dánsko a další spojence, aby darovali peníze dělostřeleckým granátům, které Estonsko koupí pro ukrajinskou armádu.

Pak ministr obrany Troels Lund Poulsen (V) podepsal o rok později slib daru více než 300 milionů DKK pro estonský nákup zbraní.

Podle několika estonských médií Estonsko rychle utratilo 71 milionů DäK dánského daru za granáty do vyprazdňujících se ukrajinských skladů munice, o nichž estonský ministr obrany tvrdil, že je rychle zaplní.

Danwatch případ přezkoumal a nyní může říci, že na Ukrajinu nebyl za peníze Dánů doručen ani jeden granát. 

To potvrdilo několik estonských státních úředníků nejprve novinách Postimees a  Estonsko zažalovalo původce toho případu. 

Samotný Danwatch tento proces potvrdil několika zdroji.

71 milionů dánských daňových dolarů místo toho skončilo u podezřelé italské společnosti s názvem Datasel, která oficiálně sdílí kancelářskou komunitu s prodejcem Audi ve městě La Spezia, a která je vlastněna indickým samozvaným výrobcem munice.

Indičtí majitelé nyní odmítají peníze vrátit.

Do 23. dubna 2025, kdy si Troels Lund Poulsen potřásl rukou, aby poslal několik milionů korun do estonského dělostřeleckého programu pro Ukrajinu, podepsalo estonské ministerstvo obrany již dvě smlouvy s Dataselem.

Stalo se tak v srpnu a říjnu 2024, kdy Estonsko předplatilo 187 milionů dánských korun za munici.

Datasel nedodal jediný granát a tím porušil smlouvy, ale když Estonci dostali peníze od dánské vlády, přesto společnosti poslali další zálohu. 

Tentokrát se 71 miliony dánských korun.

„Vyžaduje to prohlášení ministrů obrany. 
Jak od Troels Lund Poulsen, kteří uzavřeli dohodu s Estonskem, tak od Jeppeho Bruuse, který se bude muset podívat na to, jak budou dary probíhat v budoucnu. 
Možná jsou ministři bez viny, ale je třeba to prošetřit, zda je současná kontrola dostatečně dobrá," říká Frederik Waage.

Troels Lund Poulsen (V) jako Jeppe Bruus si nepřejí případ řešit.

Společnost Datasel ani její indická mateřská společnost Neco Defence nikdy nevyráběly dělostřelecké granáty.

Až do roku 2024, kdy firmu koupil indický výrobce zbraní, neměla na svých webových stránkách jediné slovo o munici. 

Ve skutečnosti je Datalet registrován jako softwarová společnost.

Dodnes je společnost certifikována jako softwarový vývojář v italském obchodním rejstříku a nemá žádné povolení vyrábět nebo prodávat zbraně.

Estonští státní auditoři už dva roky po sobě kritizují ministerstvo obrany země za to, že v souvislosti s nahromaděním tápalo s velkými částkami peněz – a tedy nejen v případě Dataselu.

Danwatch se proto také snažil získat odpovědi o tom, kde skončil zbytek dánského daru do dělostřeleckého fondu, který je kromě sporných 71 milionů korun navíc 246 milionů korun.

Ale ani ministerstvo obrany v Dánsku, ani RKIK v Estonsku to nechtějí informovat. 
Místo toho Dánsko odkazuje na Estonsko, které nesmí odpovědět na otázky kvůli dohodě o mlčenlivosti s dánským ministerstvem obrany.

Když Datasel získal Indian Neco Defence, celá společnost se změnila navenek. 

Ze dne na den byla softwarová společnost Datasel náhle popsána jako preferovaný dodavatel munice v Itálii, která navíc obchodovala s velkým počtem zemí NATO.

Pod stránkou „o nás“ například ukázala očividně počítačově animovaný snímek pěti stíhaček pod heslem „kvalifikovaný dealer“. 

Snímek však byl vytržen z přední části téměř dvacet let staré hry Xbox „Ace Combat 6“.

Danwatch oslovil bývalého ředitele společnosti Datasel a indické majitele Neco Defence. 
Nikdo z nich jim jejich dotazy neodpověděl.

Pensioners under the Unified Pension Scheme now have a digital way to submit their annual life certificate. PFRDA just launched the UPS Jeewan Setu facility on the Protean eGov mobile app. It uses Aadhaar-based face authentication, no physical form, no bank visit.

Here is what I think: the loser in this story is the pensioner who forgets the deadline. The winner is the system itself. PFRDA has set 30 November as the cut-off every year. Miss it, and your monthly payout stops. No grace period mentioned, no manual fallback in the circular.

The numbers worth knowing: UPS guarantees 50% of average basic pay from the last 12 months, with a minimum of ₹10,000 a month after 10 years of service. That minimum alone comes to ₹1.2 lakh a year per pensioner. Multiply across thousands of central government employees, and the cost of a missed deadline is real money flowing out of household cash flow for months until rectified.

What still does not add up to me: what happens if the face authentication fails? PFRDA did not say. Aadhaar-based biometrics are not perfect, especially for older pensioners whose fingerprints or facial features may have changed. They have made it convenient, but they have not told us the backup plan. That is the detail I would want before trusting the app.

🇩🇰 🇺🇦 Denmark paid for artillery shells for Ukraine. The money went to an Italian software firm that never delivered one

Denmark's defense minister confirmed on Friday that about 71 million Danish kroner, roughly 9.5 million euros, meant to buy artillery shells for Ukraine ended up with a company that delivered none. Jeppe Bruus said in written answers, reported by Ritzau and the Estonian daily Postimees, that Estonia, which handled the purchase, has agreed to return the Danish money, "the majority already now," and the rest regardless of how a lawsuit against the supplier ends. The confirmation follows an investigation published Thursday by the Danish outlet Danwatch.

The money went through an Estonian-run fund. In April 2025 Denmark donated 317 million kroner to Estonia's artillery initiative for Ukraine, according to Danwatch and Berlingske. Estonia paid 71 million kroner of it as a prepayment to Datasel, an Italian company owned by India's Neco Defence. Danwatch reports that Datasel is registered in Italy as a software developer, has no license to make or sell weapons, and shares an office address with an Audi dealer in La Spezia. After the Indian takeover in 2024, its website advertised ammunition using AI-generated images and a picture lifted from the Xbox game Ace Combat 6. Estonia's defense investment agency confirmed to Danwatch that 9.5 million euros in Datasel prepayments were "linked to funding from donor countries."

The warning signs were already there. Danwatch says Estonia had signed two contracts with Datasel in August and October 2024 and prepaid 187 million kroner without receiving a shell, then sent a further prepayment using the Danish money. Estonia is now suing the company, whose Indian owners refuse to pay the money back, according to Danwatch. The affair cost Estonian Defense Minister Hanno Pevkur his job in September. A Danish law professor, Frederik Waage, told Danwatch the national audit office should examine the case and whether there are others like it.

The sums are small next to Europe's war budgets, but the lesson is large. Europe is pooling money and routing purchases through partner governments to feed Ukraine quickly, and every middleman adds a place where checks can fail. 

This is the kind of case that critics of Ukraine aid will seize on, and the Danish response, a guaranteed refund plus pressure for an audit, is the counterargument: the system caught it, late. Denmark has not said where the remaining 246 million kroner of the donation went, and Estonia cites a confidentiality agreement.

On the video below, posted on May 2025, by @Gerashchenko_en, Mads Mikkelsen explains why the Danes are considered the happiest nation in the world. They just didn't count on a corrupt system. https://t.co/O2pzmd1520

🇩🇰 🇳🇪 🇪🇪 Creators of a website featuring imagery from video games received tens of millions from the Danish budget - a fact only now noticed by Danish media.

Copenhagen transferred $47.2 million to Estonia for the purchase of artillery shells for Ukraine. Of this amount, $10.6 million ended up with an Italian company called Datasel, which failed to deliver a single round. The contracts were signed in 2024, and the funds were transferred in 2025.

The shrewd Indian owners of Neco Defence, who acquired Datasel, populated the company’s website with visuals taken from video games. The "About Us" page featured fighter jets from the cover of *Ace Combat 6*, while the images of tanks were lifted from a website offering free wallpapers. Furthermore, Datasel is registered as a software developer and holds no license for the manufacture of weapons.

It is worth noting that this scandal - involving the procurement of ammunition for Kyiv from the very same firm - led to the ousting of Estonian Defense Minister Hanno Pevkur on September 3.

The model was meticulously crafted at ECL’s Neamatpur Central Workshop under the ‘Waste to Wealth’ initiative of Special Campaign 6. The creation showcases the ingenuity and craftsmanship of ECL’s workforce while promoting resource reutilisation and sustainability.

On behalf of Dr. Satish Jha, Chairman-cum-Managing Director, ECL, the Functional Directors and the entire ECL Parivar, Maj. S. Tiwari, Chief of Security, ECL, accompanied by Ms. Nishchal Soni, Manager (HR), Neamatpur Central Workshop, presented the model to Commodore Caesar Basu and Commander Sanjib Saran of the Indian Navy as a gesture of gratitude and respect.

From the depths of coal mines to the vast expanse of the seas, the spirit of serving the nation unites us all.

An index gaining 0.5% while nearly 70% of stocks decline is hardly a broad-based recovery.

This looks more like selective institutional rotation than a genuine market-wide reversal.

Until market breadth improves and midcaps and smallcaps start participating, I would treat every index recovery with caution.

#ECL #TeamECL #CIL #CoalIndia

The Mahanadi Coalfields IPO is an OFS. Every rupee of that ₹10,000 crore goes to Coal India, not to the coal miner itself.

That distinction matters. A fresh issue puts money into the company for capex or debt paydown. An OFS means existing holders cashing out. Here, the seller is the parent PSU, and the company gets zero from its own listing.

Mahanadi produced 218 million tonnes in FY26, about 21% of India’s coal output. Solid numbers. But you are buying shares from Coal India, not funding Mahanadi’s growth.

I find this interesting because it means the valuation depends entirely on what the market thinks Mahanadi is worth as a standalone entity, not on any new investment story. The parent gets the liquidity, and you get a separately traded PSU.

If the company needed capital, I would look closer. Here, the question is whether the price leaves room after the parent unlocks value. That is the only number that decides it for me. ⛏️
